images.title: Multiple of 4 plus 4q + 2 leaves 2 over
images.purpose: Shows that adding a multiple of 4 to an even number that is not one always leaves 2 dots over.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Three dot grids in one row with a plus sign and an equals sign between them.
images.exact_structure: Grid 1: 1 row of 4 teal (#0072B2) dots, labelled 4 above. A plus sign. Grid 2: 1 row of 4 teal (#0072B2) dots and a second row of 2 amber (#E69F00) dots at its left, labelled 6 above. An equals sign. Grid 3: 2 full rows of 4 teal (#0072B2) dots and a third row of 2 amber (#E69F00) dots at its left, labelled 10 above, 10 dots in all. A reddish purple (#CC79A7) ring around the 2 amber dots of grid 3 with the label 2 left over under it. All dots the same size. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: 4p + (4q + 2) is 4(p + q) + 2, so 2 dots are always left over and the sum is never a multiple of 4.
images.description: Shows that adding a multiple of 4 to an even number that is not one always leaves 2 dots over.

image_decisions.why: Joining a full grid with a grid that has 2 left over shows why the mixed sum is never a multiple of 4.
